Coverage, provenance, and source limits

Source: vignettes/coverage.Rmd
coverage.Rmd

The package retrieves public ArcGIS data; it does not host or archive the records. This dashboard describes the selective checked catalog bundled with this package. It never represents a complete inventory of any publisher’s datasets.

The checked catalog lists layers curated for direct use by ID. A successful health check means one layer’s endpoint and metadata passed a recent check; it does not establish that its records are fresh or that a full download will succeed. Live discovery searches publisher portals for additional items when you call it. Portal indexing, service availability, and search limits affect those results, so neither this dashboard nor live discovery measures complete publisher coverage.

Methodology and known gaps

Counts and publisher names come directly from the bundled checked catalog at site build time. This page uses the latest usable health report when one is supplied to the build. A report row must match the current catalog publisher, jurisdiction, dataset ID, and ArcGIS endpoint. A result is healthy or problematic only when it is no older than 30 days and no older than the catalog’s dated check. Recent unavailable, schema_changed, and unsupported results count as problematic. unknown, older, mismatched, and absent results are unverified. A timeout alone remains inconclusive. The last verification column labels catalog checks separately from health reports; catalog dates never imply a recent successful health check.

Some publisher datasets have not been curated into the checked catalog. Publisher portals and services may be only partly represented, and discovery can miss unindexed or unavailable items. The dashboard counts layers without a saved schema baseline; those layers cannot receive a field and geometry comparison until a baseline is curated. Health checks read layer metadata and do not run record count or object-ID queries. Each dataset’s notes include its curated scope limits and relevant recent failure diagnostics. The catalog policy records selection criteria; the discovery article explains live search limits.

Interpret source scope before analysis

Tampa’s permits and development cases are active views, not complete historical ledgers. Its city-boundary follows a shoreline representation, not a legal survey, and water-service-area extends beyond city limits. Clearwater’s park buffers are not park footprints; its critical-assets layer locates assets, not hazards. The Pinellas housing layer is a program inventory, not all housing. Hillsborough transit routes are not a live schedule. The regional planning council’s storm surge layer is a historical planning model, not current emergency guidance.

These layers alone do not establish legal boundaries, road restrictions, service eligibility, or facility status. Comparable demographic coverage and current flood and environmental coverage across all six publishers remain limited. Inspect each layer’s scope_note and source metadata for its own limits. The current Tampa fire-stations source uses unqualified fields such as NAME; older joined GIS.GovServiceInfo.* fields are unavailable.

library(tampaBayOpenData)

info <- tbod_dataset_info("construction-permits")
info[c("title", "source_url", "scope_note", "terms", "verified")]

The output is a named list about one dataset, not a table of permit records. source_url takes you to the publisher’s source page; scope_note helps decide whether the records can answer your question, and terms describes reuse conditions. These are reasons to inspect metadata before downloading.

verified records an endpoint check, not feature freshness. A portal item’s modified date can also differ from its records’ dates; modified_source distinguishes live item timestamps from saved catalog snapshots.

Discovered items may change, disappear, or lack clear reuse terms. Inspect their source metadata and publisher terms. The checked catalog remains available offline if a live portal fails.

Keep provenance with results

tbod_provenance() reads a record attached to a retrieved tibble or sf object. It includes publisher and source URLs, portal and item ID when known, validation status, query, retrieval time, row counts, integrity method, and completeness. Direct URL retrieval has not_checked status.

projects <- tbod_get_dataset("development-cases", spatial = TRUE, out_sr = 4326)
source <- tbod_provenance(projects)
saveRDS(list(data = projects, provenance = source), "development-cases.rds")

The saved RDS file contains two named components: data is the spatial table of active case features, and provenance describes the request that produced it. This lets someone revisiting your map distinguish a change in source data from a change in your analysis.

Save provenance separately before transformations or exports that may discard attributes. A finite subset is marked incomplete when more rows match. Object-ID checks detect missing, duplicate, or unexpected records, but cannot freeze live attributes across requests. See retrieval and downloads for the integrity methods.

Monitoring and evidence

Use tbod_check_catalog() for a current metadata and schema check of the bundled catalog, or pass ids to inspect selected layers:

health <- tbod_check_catalog(ids = c("construction-permits", "stpete-parks"))
health[, c("dataset_id", "status", "schema_status", "details")]

In the displayed columns, dataset_id identifies the entry, status gives the overall check result, schema_status describes the structure comparison, and details explains the result. Use these together to decide which source needs inspection rather than treating every unsuccessful check as the same problem.

This contacts the publishers and returns one row per checked entry. Statuses include healthy, unavailable, schema_changed, unsupported, and unknown; transient failures remain unknown after bounded retries. Inspect schema_issues for field or geometry changes and failure_type and the service and layer status columns for request failures. The check reads layer metadata and does not run count or object-ID queries. A healthy row describes that moment’s endpoint and schema; it does not certify record freshness, full retrieval support, or future availability.

Twice weekly monitoring checks the selected layers in the checked catalog, bounded live discovery, and county facility retrieval by descriptor and stable ID. It also checks server projection to EPSG:4326. Retrievals request at most two rows; scans inspect at most one service item per publisher. The test guide describes these bounds and the manual live suite. The validation record dates completed checks; they cannot guarantee future availability or record freshness.

A separate weekly catalog health workflow uses tbod_check_catalog() and uploads timestamped RDS, CSV, and Markdown reports. It does not change the bundled catalog.

Cite the package and its data sources

For published work, cite the package version you used. R provides citation text and BibTeX after installation:

citation("tampaBayOpenData")
toBibtex(citation("tampaBayOpenData"))

Cite the original data publisher and dataset separately. tbod_dataset_info(id) gives source details; tbod_provenance(result) records source and retrieval time. The MIT license applies to the package software, not government datasets. Publishers set their data terms. The package is independent of them and of rOpenSci.

For implementation details, see the architecture and research basis.
